test_window.relation: disjoint group (held-out locations / sentinel landscapes), not a time window and not an iid split
evidence: no date/time column exists in training.csv or sorted_test.csv, so a future-window relation is ruled out

the 15 spatial covariates (BSAN..TMFI) act as a location fingerprint: 580 unique tuples over 1157 train rows and 368 over 727 test rows, with the modal tuple appearing exactly twice (565 train / 353 test) matching a Topsoil+Subsoil pair sampled at one location; Depth counts (train 581/576, test 368/359) agree
zero exact spatial-tuple overlap and zero PIDN overlap between train and test

test locations sit systematically far from train locations in the 15-d spatial covariate space: train->train nearest-neighbour distance median 0.306 (95th pct 0.974) vs test->train median 0.956, and 46.7% of test locations exceed the train 95th percentile — consistent with test locations drawn from geographic clusters absent from train, not from the same clusters

split_policy.scheme: GroupKFold with the group key = the 15-covariate spatial tuple (location); prefer a coarser landscape group (cluster the spatial tuples) so that same-neighbourhood locations cannot straddle folds, which better mimics the observed train/test location gap
split_policy.forbidden: plain shuffled KFold on rows — it puts the Topsoil and Subsoil sample of the same location in different folds (near-duplicate spectra, same site covariates) and gives an optimistic CV that will not transfer to held-out landscapes
split_policy.notes: 5 folds is adequate at n=1157; evaluate with leave-fold-out honest MCRMSE (blend weights fit on out-of-fold data only, never in-sample)

metric.name: MCRMSE
metric.definition: mean over the 5 target columns of the columnwise RMSE
traps: equal weight per target regardless of difficulty: a single hard target (P) can dominate the achievable headroom, so per-target modelling and per-target blend weights matter more than a single global model
RMSE family, not MAE family — use L2 objectives; TASK-MAE-METRIC does not apply

targets are pre-standardized but heavily right-skewed (skew Ca 4.71, P 7.45, SOC 2.45, pH 0.87, Sand 0.39) so squared error is driven by a handful of extreme rows; a fold that happens to hold the extremes swings the fold score
targets contain negative values, so any log-type transform needs a shift and an exact inverse inside the metric evaluation
blend weights for an RMSE-family metric have an NNLS closed form — random/Dirichlet weight search leaves ~1e-5 on the table

external_data.rationale: no whitelist source has a usable join key in this data: there is no country, no date, no currency, and no raw geographic coordinate — the spatial covariates are anonymized derived rasters (BSAN/BSAS/BSAV/CTI/ELEV/EVI/LSTD/LSTN/REF*/RELI/TMAP/TMFI) with no published lookup back to lat/lon. Whitelist rule (1) — join keys must exist in the official data or be derivable from it — fails for all five sources.

rejected_from_whitelist.reason: join key is country x year; neither column exists nor is derivable
join key is country x date; no date column
no country identifier in the data
join key is currency x month; not applicable
2020+ daily country series; this is a 2014 soil-sampling dataset with no date or country

data_level: treat the 3578 m*-columns as an ordered signal, not as independent features: Savitzky-Golay smoothing and 1st/2nd derivatives (window ~21-31) plus SNV / row-wise standard-normal-variate normalization
fit dimensionality reduction (PCA / PLS components) on the spectra strictly inside each training fold, never on the full matrix, since n is small enough that fold leakage is measurable
derive an explicit location group key from the 15-covariate tuple and carry it through every split as the GroupKFold key; it is also the pairing key for the Topsoil/Subsoil pair
trim spectral regions found in EDA to be near-constant or saturated across all rows — they add p without signal in a p >> n regime (identify empirically, do not hardcode)
encode Depth as a binary and consider a Depth x spectral-component interaction; the two depths of the same location carry different chemistry from the same landscape covariates

the 15 spatial covariates are the only true site-level features and are heavily reused (2 rows per tuple) — keep them but do not let a model memorize them, since test sites are outside the train covariate neighbourhood
model_level: per-target models (5 independent fits) rather than one multi-output fit, because MCRMSE weights each column equally and the targets have very different difficulty and skew
regularized linear/kernel families over GBDT for p >> n: Kernel Ridge with RBF kernel, SVR, PLS regression, plus Ridge as a floor
add one shallow, heavily-regularized, structurally-different member as a decorrelator before optimizing blend weights (TASK-BLEND-DECOR)
solve blend weights per target with NNLS (closed form for RMSE family) on out-of-fold predictions only
avoid learned stacking meta-models: with n=1157 and grouped folds the meta-learner has very few effective independent samples

unmatched_task_priors_checked: TASK-TS-FUTURE (no date column, test is not a future window)
TASK-TS-CALENDAR (no daily series, no store/product keys)
TASK-STRUCT-OUT (5 independent scalar targets, no generative grid/sequence rule)
eda_must_verify: confirm the location-group hypothesis: cluster the 15 spatial covariates and check that the resulting clusters are disjoint between train and test at the cluster level, not only at the exact-tuple level
confirm no nulls across all 3594 feature columns (only a subset was inspected at this stage)
quantify the honest CV penalty of GroupKFold vs shuffled KFold on one cheap baseline to size the optimism bias
identify empirically which spectral regions are constant/saturated before trimming
not_recorded: official competition rules text on whether external data is permitted — not present in config.yaml and not resolvable without fetching the rules page; moot here because external_data.needed is 'no'
true geographic coordinates or sentinel-landscape identifiers — not provided in the data; the location grouping is inferred from spatial-covariate tuples only
the exact sampling design (how many landscapes, how sites were assigned to train vs test) — stated only in the competition description, not derivable from the files inspected
physical units and the standardization constants of the targets — the values are pre-standardized with no de-standardization key provided
